item.title: WSIB Cuts Employer Registration from Days to Minutes With Guidewire
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Ontario’s Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB, Toronto) has modernized its employer-registration process using Guidewire (San Mateo, Calif.) Jutro Digital Platform, reducing a process that previously took eight to 10 business days to under 10 minutes for most applicants. “We wanted the employer registration process to be simple and intuitive while freeing our teams to focus on the complex cases that require human judgment,” comments Greg Morreale, VP, Enterprise Technology Solutions, WSIB. WSIB and Guidewire position the registration project as the digital foundation for future AI capabilities rather than an AI deployment in itself.

item.title: Payment Friction Is a Persistency Issue for Life Insurers
item.description: When payment friction contributes to preventable lapses, carriers lose premium revenue, policyholder lifetime value and future growth opportunities. When payment processes create unnecessary friction, distribution organizations spend time managing administrative issues instead of strengthening customer relationships and generating new business. How often do payment problems create friction between advisors and clients?

item.title: France Says Iran’s Revolutionary Guards Carried Out Fridge Hacks
item.description: “The responsibility for this attack lies with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps,” French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said on Monday in Paris, in a rare direct attribution of the hacks to a foreign power. France has openly pointed the finger at Iran for recent cyberattacks that crippled fridges and created havoc in hundreds of supermarkets across the nation. Related: US Warns of ‘Ongoing Cyber Threat’ to Industrial Refrigeration Systems Barrot, who was speaking on the sidelines of an informal G7 ministerial meeting, said he would be seeking retaliatory measures against Iran and has summoned the country’s ambassador about the matter.

item.description: They also intend to jointly develop products combining insurance coverage with mobility services and connect their distribution networks across online and physical channels. item.title: Manulife John Hancock plans private markets retirement funds
item.description: Manulife John Hancock Retirement is partnering with Great Gray Trust Company to develop Lifetime Blend+, a proposed suite of target-date collective investment trusts that would give defined contribution retirement plan participants exposure to private markets. As of September 30, 2026, Manulife John Hancock Retirement serviced more than 56,000 retirement plans covering over 3.3 million participants, with more than $278 billion in assets under management and administration. The funds would be available only through eligible retirement plans, with private-market exposure carrying risks including limited liquidity, valuation complexity and higher fees.

item.title: Acceptiv brings Amore life insurance quotes to ChatGPT
item.description: Canadian insurance technology company Acceptiv has introduced Amore Insurance Quick Quote, a ChatGPT app that provides term life insurance quotes for eligible Canadian applicants. Acceptiv, founded in 2014 by Kevin Pledge, develops RiskDX, a digital life insurance distribution platform covering quotes, applications, automated underwriting, electronic signatures and policy delivery. The app checks available coverage amounts and policy terms, calculates premiums and creates shareable quotes.

item.title: US Opens Probe into Waymo Vehicles Over School Bus Safety Violations
item.description: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Monday it had opened a recall query into 2,895 vehicles operated by Alphabet’s self-driving unit Waymo over continued traffic safety violations involving the vehicles’ behavior when encountering school buses. The probe will determine whether a software fix Waymo rolled out late last year failed to stop its driverless cars from passing school buses with flashing red lights, as most of the violations happened after the company said the remedy was fully deployed. Separately, NHTSA had opened a probe in January after one of Waymo’s self-driving vehicles struck a child near an elementary school in Santa Monica, California.

item.title: Adaptive Insurance CTO Sees a Future for Parametric in Homeowners
item.description: For Adaptive, which began with parametric power outage coverage and has expanded its focus to flood, wind, hail and other specialty exposures, he sees opportunity in filling those gaps rather than attempting to replace a standard homeowners policy. The homeowners insurance policy of the future may look more like a collection of coverage options to meet each policyholder’s specific needs rather than one singular solution. At least, that’s the direction envisioned by Arik Yelovitch, chief technology officer and co-founder of Adaptive Insurance.

item.title: Paper Unicorns Are Cheap. Building A $1B Revenue AI Company Takes A Multimarket Cap Table
item.description: Having studied in China before building an AI company in Abu Dhabi, I have also seen how the same growth story can raise different questions among investors, eventually boiling down to: “What will customers keep paying for?” Fast revenue deserves attention. I would set a higher benchmark for unicorns with $1 billion in revenue sustained by customers who keep paying. A $1 billion valuation still makes a startup a unicorn on paper.

item.title: Series A In 2026: Capital Is Flowing Faster, But Fewer Startups Are Making The Cut
item.description: (At Series B, too, we’re seeing a similar trend of fewer but larger deals.) That leaves companies still proving their growth potential navigating a Series A funding crunch even as capital floods into the fastest-growing businesses. More money is pouring into Series A rounds, but it isn’t opening the door to more startups. AI is fueling demand for capital and helping some startups grow at unprecedented speeds, while others struggle to turn their first customers into repeatable sales.

item.title: VKB seeks reduced pricing for King Max Re German multi-peril cat bond renewal
item.description: German domestic market insurance group VKB is now aiming to secure its first renewal of a catastrophe bond at reduced pricing, with the price guidance now lowered for the still €175 million King Max Re II DAC (Series 2026-1) German multi-peril transaction, we understand from sources. The company had sponsored its debut cat bond in late 2023, securing €175 million of multi-peril catastrophe reinsurance protection from the King Max Re DAC 2023 issuance, which is scheduled to mature in early January 2027. Versicherungskammer Bayern Versicherungsanstalt des oeffentlichen Rechts’ (VKB) returned to the catastrophe bond market for its second sponsorship in October, with the transaction a renewal of sorts for its soon to mature debut issuance.

item.title: Hannover Re plans to renew similar retro structures for 2027, in line with growth: Althoff
item.description: This morning, when asked about the retro renewal, Althoff explained, “We are planning to place very similar retro structures in line also with the underlying growth of our business, so no changes intended on that side.” Hannover Re has been growing this year, so this does suggest that the retro program could increase in size for 2027. Hannover Re is looking towards its renewal of retrocessional protection for 2027 with a plan to place similar structures to the current program, while it seems there could be some increase given the underwriting growth of the company. Althoff was also asked about the potential for further underwriting growth into property catastrophe reinsurance at the January 2027 renewals and said that it will depend on market conditions.

item.title: UCITS cat bond fund returns hit 7.87% YTD after October. 12-month declines again: Plenum Index
item.description: Catastrophe bond funds structured as UCITS investment strategies delivered strong returns in October to end the month with a 7.87% return for 2026 so far, while the rolling-twelve month average performance has declined further, according to the Plenum CAT Bond UCITS Fund Indices . 2026 remains on-track to see at the least the fourth highest annual return for UCITS cat bond funds, according to specialist catastrophe bond and insurance bond investment manager Plenum Investment’s Index, which tracks this cat bond fund sector back to 2011. The latest data from the Plenum Index is for the period September 25th through October 31st 2026 and across this period the average return of the UCITS catastrophe bond funds reached 1.12%.

item.title: MSIG UK launches Construction and Marine Cargo classes
item.description: MSIG UK, the UK arm of global insurance group MSIG, has announced the launch of dedicated Construction and Marine Cargo classes, expanding its London Market and UK product capabilities. Tim Harris, acting Chief Underwriting Officer at MSIG UK, said, “The launch of Construction and Marine Cargo represents another important step in the development of our UK business. Andrew Morris will join MSIG UK on 9 November 2026 as Head of Construction, reporting to Paul Keaveney, Head of Non-Marine.

item.title: Hong Kong general insurance premiums rise 8% as health and property demand strengthens, says AM Best
item.description: Hong Kong’s general insurance industry generated gross written premiums (GWP) of HK $108.5 billion in 2025, an increase of 8% compared with the previous year, according to AM Best, an international credit rating agency specialising in the insurance sector. In its report, Health and Property Lines Drive Hong Kong’s Non-Life Insurance Growth, AM Best identified continued competition as a significant feature of the territory’s non-life insurance market. According to AM Best, accident and health (A&H) policies represented 37% of market premiums, while property damage and general liability, including employees’ compensation insurance, retained broadly unchanged shares between 2024 and 2025.

item.title: QBE Insurance appoints Nigel Hawtin as Chief Transformation & Operations Officer
item.description: QBE Insurance, an international insurance and reinsurance group, has announced the appointment of Nigel Hawtin as Chief Transformation & Operations Officer for its Australia Pacific business, effective 10 December 2026, subject to regulatory approval. He has a deep understanding of our business and how operations and transformation connect, and I’m delighted to welcome him to our Executive Management Board.” QBE Insurance confirmed that Hawtin will join its Executive Management Board as part of the appointment, bringing his experience in claims, operations and transformation to the senior leadership team. Having joined the company in 2016, he has held a range of senior leadership positions spanning claims management, operations and business transformation.

item.title: GM Insurance to Enter Maryland Auto Market
item.description: GM Insurance announced it is expanding its auto insurance offering to Maryland, which will be its 21 st state. GM Insurance will now be available in the following states: Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas Virginia and Wisconsin. General Motors Insurance is available for Chevrolet, Buick, GMC and Cadillac vehicles., GM promises that its coverage can save safe drivers money with its connected technology that collects data about driving behavior and operation of the vehicle.

item.title: AI Backlash Spreads Across Europe With Data Center Protests
item.description: Protests against data centers continued across Europe on Saturday as citizens took to the streets to voice their concerns about the impact on society and the environment. and Alphabet Inc.’s Google that turned the country into a major data center hub, one of Europe’s biggest. Representatives from Stop Dirty Data Centres , a coalition of local democracy and climate protest groups, said they aimed to “halt the unchecked expansion of AI data centers and prevent our democracy being taken hostage by big tech industry interests.” Campaign groups from Scotland to Spain and France to Denmark joined the action calling for a moratorium to pause construction “until we, the people, have democratically decided what is needed to ensure AI and data centers serve people and the planet, not private greed.” Saturday’s protests followed a demonstration in Amsterdam on Friday, when hundreds of protesters clashed with police at a Microsoft Corp.

item.description: Kaiser Ng, the chief financial officer at Binance Holdings Ltd., the world’s largest crypto exchange, is leaving, the company announced just days after hackers stole more than $6 billion in cryptocurrency from the platform. Related: Binance $6.3 Billion Heist to Prompt Closer Scrutiny by Insurers Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance last week in the biggest heist in cryptocurrency’s history. item.description: Kalepa has raised $75m in Series B funding at a $470m valuation, led by Updata Partners, according to a company announcement dated 5 November 2026. Kalepa performs and orchestrates insurance workflows across operations, underwriting, pricing, and portfolio management, and said its insurance-specific AI coordinates agents with human expertise or approval where needed. This funding lets us bring Professional Grade AI to more of the work insurers do, so they have that choice across the entire value chain," said Paul Monasterio, co-founder and CEO of Kalepa.

item.title: Samsung Fire, KKR and KIC to buy UK Insurer Canopius
item.description: According to reports, Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance will acquire a controlling stake in UK specialty insurer Canopius for about $2.2 billion in partnership with private equity firm KKR and the Korea Investment Corporation. Samsung Fire & Marine currently owns 40% of Canopius. Once the deal closes, Samsung Fire & Marine’s stake is expected to rise to about 79%, with KKR holding 13% and KIC 8%.

item.title: GEICO Q3 underwriting profit drops to $982 million
item.description: GEICO’s pre-tax underwriting earnings fell 45% in the third quarter of 2026 to $982 million, from $1.77 billion a year earlier, according to Berkshire Hathaway’s Q3 report published November 7, 2026. Underwriting expenses rose 17% in the quarter. As a side note, GEICO ended 2025 with 29,541 employees, up from 28,247 in 2024 but down 30% from a peak of 42,156 in 2020.

item.title: Assurant acquires Protection Point Service Plans
item.description: Assurant has acquired Protection Point Service Plans, a British Columbia-based provider and administrator of commercial equipment protection programs. Protection Point specializes in extended service plans and related protection for equipment used in agriculture, construction, material handling and forestry. The acquisition builds on an existing relationship: Protection Point already worked exclusively with Assurant’s Canadian commercial equipment business, with Assurant underwriting its programs.

item.title: Berkshire Hathaway underwriting earnings fall 43% in Q3 as Tokio Marine deal supports P&C reinsurance premiums
item.description: Berkshire Hathaway reported a 43% decline in net underwriting earnings across its insurance and reinsurance operations to $1.352 billion for the third quarter of 2026, while earnings for the first nine months fell 16% to $4.8 billion. The Berkshire Hathaway Reinsurance Group delivered pre-tax underwriting earnings of $582 million for Q3’26 and $1.868 billion for 9M’26, compared to $884 million in Q3’25 and $1.227 billion in 9M’25. As in the second quarter, P&C reinsurance top-line was boosted in the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 from the deal with Tokio Marine, under which NICO assumes on a quota share basis a portion of the non-life premiums written and related losses and expenses of the Japanese insurer on risks attaching over a 10-year term.

item.title: Automation Anywhere to acquire Boost.ai
item.description: Automation Anywhere has agreed to acquire conversational AI company Boost.ai from Nordic Capital, adding customer-facing chat and voice capabilities to its business automation platform. “By joining Automation Anywhere, we can connect the conversation, including voice, directly to the systems and people who get the work done, so a customer’s request is handled from start to finish.” – Jerry Haywood, CEO of Boost.ai. Automation Anywhere plans to connect those conversations to the systems and workflows needed to complete customer requests.

item.title: Trucordia expands BYU sponsorship
item.description: Trucordia has expanded its corporate sponsorship of Brigham Young University Athletics under a multiyear agreement that adds the insurance brokerage’s logo to BYU football helmet bumpers. “We’re proud to deepen our sponsorship with BYU Athletics.” – Felix Morgan, Trucordia’s CEO and chairman. Headquartered in Lindon, Utah, Trucordia has sponsored BYU Athletics since 2024.

item.title: AmeriLife Selects Palantir for Enterprise AI Transformation
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) AmeriLife (Clearwater, Fla.) has selected Palantir Technologies (Aventura, Fla.) for an enterprise-wide AI and data initiative spanning its Health and Wealth distribution organizations. The agreement brings Palantir Foundry and Artificial Intelligence Platform, or AIP, into AmeriLife’s operations with the goal of creating a common data foundation and supporting AI-driven workflows across distribution, case management and back-office functions. “Partnering with Palantir, which is widely trusted with some of the most complex and consequential data challenges in the world, allows us to rebuild how our business runs, from the first client conversation to the placed policy.” AmeriLife says the initiative is intended to go beyond adding AI tools to existing processes by building workflows on a unified data foundation.

item.title: ACORD’s Kellington Sees AI Opening for Industry Rethink
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) John Kellington sees the industry’s embrace of AI as an opportunity to reconsider how insurance operates—and what technology and standards must provide to support it. A Shared Vision for Change Kellington sees ACORD’s role as bringing together organizations that would struggle to establish common approaches independently. “If there’s something that I can do to help this industry get better because of my background experience,” Kellington says, “gosh, you know, that’s something everybody dreams about.” ACORD Names John Kellington CEO ACORD Adds Two Board Members

item.title: Amdocs Bets on EIS to Advance Agentic Transformation in Insurance
item.description: The telecommunications technology provider intends to combine EIS’ platform and insurance expertise with its own engineering, transformation and operational capabilities to build an insurance business centered on agentic technology and accountability for delivery. “They buy them because they believe the business case and execution plan will succeed.” Bringing aOS Into the Core A central element of Amdocs’ strategy is extending aOS, its agentic operating system developed for telecommunications, into insurance. (Image source: EIS powered by Amdocs homepage.) Amdocs’ acquisition of EIS gives the insurance core systems vendor more than a larger balance sheet.

item.title: California Homes Face Shutoffs as Santa Anas Raise Fire Risks
item.description: Thousands of homes and businesses north of Los Angeles face the risk of potential power cuts over the next two days as weak to moderate Santa Ana winds bring dangerous fire weather conditions. Southern California Edison is considering shutting off power to 4,639 homes and businesses in Los Angeles County, as well as another 297 in Ventura County, the utility said on its website. California has entered the most perilous stretch of its year-round fire season, when hot, arid winds roll down from the mountains and out to sea.

item.title: Berkshire’s Pivot to AI Bets Gets an Immediate Reality Check
item.description: After all, Buffett’s 2016 investment in Apple Inc., derided at the time as being late in the iPhone maker’s history, turned out to be one of Berkshire’s most lucrative bets. In his first year as Chief Executive Officer of Berkshire Hathaway Inc., Greg Abel has pushed the conglomerate into an entirely new area of investment: artificial intelligence. But with cracks in the AI trade starting to show, Berkshire’s sudden push may appear ill-timed.

item.title: Paris, Madrid Top Cities for Harsh Driving Events While Berlin Ranks Lowest: Study
item.description: The four cities with the highest efficiency scores, Berlin, Amsterdam, Dublin and Rome, are the four with the fewest harsh events per trip, while Paris, London and Madrid, the three lowest-scoring cities, have the three highest rates. Harsh acceleration accounts for 79% of Paris events and 69% of Madrid events, while Berlin and London split more evenly between acceleration and braking. Madrid (1,088) and Paris (1,191) sit far above the rest, at roughly one harsh event for every trip, with the gap between Berlin and Paris being 5.3 times, and between Berlin and Madrid 4.8 times.

item.title: Vantage Partnership Capital (AdVantage) drives $15m income for Howard Hughes in Q3 2026
item.description: Vantage Risk’s third-party reinsurance capital and investments platform has again delivered higher fee income to the benefit of its now owner, Bill Ackman linked Howard Hughes Holdings, with $13 million of fee income generated by its insurance-linked securities style partnerships with investors in Q3 2026 and $15 million of total net income from the ILS activities. Howard Hughes Holding stated that Q3 2026 fee income for AdVantage was, “resulting from the continued positive outcomes for recent property catastrophe business written in this structure.” Marc Grandisson, the former Arch Capital CEO who joined the Howard Hughes Holdings Board of Directors this year, commented during an earnings call today, “Net fee income was $13 million in the quarter, up from $9 million, and is $47 million year to date, versus the loss last year. It takes year-to-date fee income earned by the Vantage Partnership Capital team, operating its business through the AdVantage platform of companies, to $47 million.

item.title: Mandarin Re to establish retakaful window to deliver risk capacity to underserved markets
item.description: Mandarin Re, an international short-tail-lines reinsurer, has received regulatory approval from the Labuan Financial Services Authority to establish a retakaful window, paving the way for the company to offer Shariah-compliant reinsurance solutions globally. The newly established retakaful window operates as a dedicated Islamic division within the conventional reinsurer, allowing Mandarin Re to deliver treaties and programmes structured to support wakalah, mudharabah, and wakalah-waqf takaful providers. With the new licence, Mandarin Re is now able to help takaful operators world-wide to access additional capacity, allowing them to better serve their communities.

item.title: AM Best revises Premia Re Europe’s under review status to developing
item.description: AM Best has revised the implications of the under review status to developing from negative for the Financial Strength Rating of B++ (Good) and the Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating of “bbb” (Good) of Premia Reinsurance Europe S.A. The ratings agency explained that the revision of the under review status to developing followed Premia’s acquisition of Premia Re Europe. AM Best said the ratings of Premia Re Europe are expected to remain under review with developing implications until it gains clarity regarding the new owner’s plans for the entity.
